title: Weingart
description: A song credit set like a forme of hand-set metal type: three stepped lines of title, a process-red running time printed underneath, rules and a reversed slug, small text cascading down the right. Push any line and it moves the way lead moves in a chase, one diagonal step at a time, its letters opening out as it travels down and closing up as it climbs back. The slugs are solid: a line that runs into its neighbour shoves it a step ahead, and that one shoves the next, so one drag reflows the whole forme into a stepped cascade that bunches up and locks against the edge of the chase. Only the red, printed in its own run, crosses the black, and where they overprint the two inks make a third, darker one.
intent: After Wolfgang Weingart's Basel letterpress experiments and his stepped Typografische Monatsblätter covers (1972–73): Swiss order broken from inside the system, using the real constraints of a press, quantised steps, letterspacing and overprinting, to make new rhythm. https://neugraphic.com/weingart/weingart-text2.html
